about: Needs the traffic corpus cannot show, each with its evidence. checker/derive.py merges them into the needs index for the ranking and grade.py's eligible suites. An entry is a need a suite has, never a reason to skip it; remove one when the corpus starts showing it.

nereids_p0.cte.test_cte_filter_pushdown..reason: Its explain shape plan reads nereids_test_query_db.test, which nereids_p0/load.groovy loads; with the table empty the FE plans PhysicalEmptyRelation instead of the expected filter (doris-rs run m2-eligible-1, 2026-11-04). That load suite is outside the gate, so the index has no needs for it.

load_p0.stream_load.test_stream_load_ill.reason: The suite expects the C++ BE's stream load reply "[INVALID_ARGUMENT]Invalid format of 'timeout': 'abc', stoi", so its stream load reaches the BE, but the corpus kept no BE HTTP exchange for it (the reference traffic for this suite holds only Thrift).

load_p0.stream_load.test_stream_load_inc.reason: Its stream load sets 'where' (d = 'doris' or d = 'asf' or b = 9 or b = 8), which the FE plans as conjuncts on the file scan node; the needs index does not read the scan node's conjuncts, so the predicates it needs are declared here (doris-rs run m4-full-1, 2026-11-05). It also needs the conjuncts evaluated in the stream load itself, rows that fail them counted as unselected; doris-rs refuses a WHERE on a stream load (doris-rs run m5-full-1, 2026-11-07).

load_p0.stream_load.test_group_commit_st.reason: Its stream loads set group_commit=async_mode and the suite checks each reply is a group commit; doris-rs commits each load as its own transaction, so every reply lacks the group commit fields (doris-rs run m5-full-1, 2026-11-07). The corpus shows the loads but not the mode.

nereids_p0.stats.col_stats.hot_value_str.reason: Its ANALYZE runs the FE's statistics SQL (count, ndv, min, max), which fails on doris-rs without ndv; the explain at exchange 13 then shows other statistics (doris-rs run m5-full-1, 2026-11-07). The corpus attributes that SQL outside the suite.

nereids_p0.select_tablets.select_with_ta.reason: Exchange 37, SELECT * FROM table_no_partition with no ORDER BY, returns its two rows (one per tablet) in the C++ BE's scanner order, stable over the 5 reference runs; doris-rs returns the same rows in another order, which the strict gate compares (doris-rs run m5-full-1, 2026-11-07). Neither instance order nor tablet order reproduces it.

groups.reason: query_p0/sql_functions/conditional_functions/test_coalesce_new.groovy sets the FE config enable_date_conversion=false at line 21 and back to true at line 49; on doris-rs it fails at line 43 (an INSERT into a DATETIME v1 column), so the FE keeps creating v1 DATE/DATETIME columns, which doris-rs does not write, for every later suite. These are the eligible suites that failed on a v1 date type after it (doris-rs run m5-full-1, 2026-11-07); on the reference their tables are DATEV2/DATETIMEV2. Remove when test_coalesce_new passes line 49.
